newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy sees CPI under three pct by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Italy sees CPI under three pct by year-end.

text.p: Italy's consumer price index should show a sharp fall in October and November and an inflation level of below three percent year-on-year is a "reachable target" by the end of 1996, a treasury source said on Monday.
Data from six sample Italian cities on Monday pointed to September CPI at an annual 3.4 percent, unchanged from August, with a monthly rate of 0.3 percent.
The source said that apart from some anomalies in data from Bologna and Perugia published on Monday "today's price data is fully in line with the downward trend of inflation".
Bologna said its September consumer price index stood at 1.0 percent month-on-month and 4.2 percent year-on-year. In August, Bologna's inflation rate was flat and 3.5 percent respectively.
Perugia's numbers were 0.9 percent month-on-month and 4.1 percent year-on-year in September, compared with 0.1 percent and 3.5 percent in August.

These two cities saw a "marked increase month-on-month entirely because of soccer matches" the source added. The two cities' clubs were both promoted to Serie A (the first division) and ticket prices doubled as a result.
"On a national level, however, there will be an overall evening out with season tickets rising overall only 0.1 point," the source said.
